Definition: properly, remembered, i.e. a male (of man or animals, as being the most noteworthy sex)
BiblicalUsage: zâkâr means properly, remembered, that is a male (of man or animals, as being the most noteworthy sex). In Genesis 1:27 we read, "So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them." It appears again in Exodus 12:5: "Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year: ye shall take it out from the sheep, or from the goats:".
TheologicalSignificance: zakar is properly, remembered, that is a male (of man or animals, as being the most noteworthy sex), and I believe God does not use words carelessly, so this one does the work he gave it.
